# Open decisions, third adjudication: every question still open after the third tooling stack, adjudicated for provenance and walkability

_Written 2026-11-19 (UTC) by an Opus-class adjudicator, on the owner's instruction of 2026-11-19, relayed by the coordinator of `session_2026-11-18-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack-2`: "have Opus adjudicate all open decisions based upon long-term integrity re provenance and walkability as well as context from my prior rulings". Planning only: no script, schema, check, migration, database row, ledger line or task file was changed. Canadian English. Every figure is given as the command that produces it; re-run it. Checked against branch `ccr-cc893571-i4lug4` at `41b67411` (pull request #240, open, untouched), schema version `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute('pragma user_version').fetchone())"`. Form and discipline follow `PROPAGATION-AND-CONSOLIDATION-ADJUDICATION.md`. The ledger outranks this file._

## 0. Rule 0 on contact, and what the delegation does not reach

**The owner's instruction of today supersedes, for the items below and on contact (CLAUDE.md rule 0), every ledger sentence that said an item was not to be resolved under delegation.** Named, so the supersession is recorded and not implied: the ACTION (3) of "Owner statements 2026-11-18 — OD-71 … and OD-72 …" ("Ask the owner the open parts in their plain form; do not resolve them under delegation"); ACTION (3) of "Owner statement 2026-11-18 (third) — OD-69"; ACTION (4) of "Owner answers 2026-11-17 — OD-68 … OD-69 … OD-70"; ACTION (4) of "Correction and registration 2026-11-15" (OD-67); the "Registration 2026-11-14" sentence "None is to be resolved under delegation" (OD-62); and the referrals of 2026-11-13 (OD-46 to OD-54), which were a delegate's own referrals and never an owner's prohibition. The ledger is not edited here; the draft entry of section 4 records it.

**What the delegation does not reach.** It does not move CLAUDE.md §8: content and doctrine (mission, audience, CRPD posture, population taxonomy, evidence-tier definitions, jurisdiction, licensing, trajectory) stay the owner's to ratify. For each such item the resolution below is a **recommended default the owner must ratify**, with what is safe meanwhile. A ratification act that is the owner's by its nature (OD-17, "ratify the contract") is not adjudicable at all.

**The test applied to every item.** PROVENANCE: one home per fact; a typed value warranted by the source's own words, never by memory or a substring; nothing fabricated; history retired in place ("retire in place then", owner ruling 2026-09-16). WALKABILITY: the pipeline "can be run in all directions at any stage in such a manner where we can dynamically research, adjudicate, synthesize, specify and render across a multitude of languages and jurisdictions" (owner, 2026-11-12), with "no hard coded behaviours" and no "dead ends or whatever" (owner statements 2026-11-12 (seventh)); a rule that blocks a legitimate walk, or lets a walk reach a cell through an unwarranted step, fails.

## 1. How the list was derived

1. **The three sweep lists**, read in full: every item under "Not repaired", "Open", "Stopped", or marked OWNER'S, owner question or design question (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-15-remediation-stack/sweep-list.md`, `scratchpad/session_2026-11-16-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack/sweep-list.md`, `scratchpad/session_2026-11-18-remediation-batch-1-tooling-stack-2/sweep-list.md`; abbreviated S15, S16, S18 below with line numbers).
2. **The register**: every OD whose last status line is neither ANSWERED BY THE OWNER nor RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION with a satisfied check: `for n in $(seq -w 1 72); do grep -F "OD-$n STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1; done` and the same for `CHECK:`. Every delegated resolution's check reads `not required` or `confirmed with corrections applied`. Open: OD-17 (DEFERRED BY THE OWNER), OD-46, OD-47, OD-48, OD-51, OD-52, OD-54, OD-62, OD-67, OD-69, OD-72 (REFERRED BACK), and OD-71's "not decided" residue.
3. **Every ledger `REFERRED BACK TO THE OWNER`**: `grep -n "REFERRED BACK" references/project-standards.md`; each id whose latest status still reads so is in (2).
4. **Pull request #240's eleven "Open owner questions"** (read through `gh api repos/jordanelias/guidebook/pulls/240`); each maps onto an S18 item.

Items that are a limit, a datum or a process note rather than a decision are numbered in the table and marked LIMIT, with their disposition in one line; only decisions get the six-part adjudication. Items that later commits already closed are marked CLOSED with the evidence.

    tables and views (`v_research_scope`, `v_scan_ledger`, `v_live_lens_links`, ...), never typed, so a run
    started mid-pipeline can read what to skip and what to do. Read-only: nothing is written.

    A pair's scope is reported as it stands in `lang_jur_map.scope_status`: a NULL is reported as
    `scope_unrecorded` (owed, as `v_research_scope` reads it), never as in scope or out of it."""
    given = {"identity_code": identity, "icf_code": icf, "needs_code": needs}
    lens = {k: v for k, v in given.items() if v}

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m -q --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

## 12. Repair after the adversarial pass (2026-11-20)

Compensating migration `scripts/migrations/163_gap_resolution_kind.sql` (162 is not edited): a fourth cell `resolution_kind` (CHECK IN its kinds, present exactly when the other three are; `close-gap --resolution-kind` reads the kinds with `dbcore.check_values`), and the stamp's hour and minute by shape (`datetime()` round-trips hour 24). `close-gap` checks each pointer by its kind: a commit must exist in this repository (`git cat-file -e`; with no git it refuses and names the next act), a ledger pointer must be well formed with its quote found once, a task id must have its file, a duplicate must name another gap that exists, and a reason is words (a pointer of another kind given as a reason is refused). The data migration path is no longer offered: the migration that carries a closing is emitted after it. The status must have the closing shape every live status has (`select distinct status from gaps where status like 'CLOSED%'`). The UPDATE is guarded (`AND status LIKE 'OPEN%'`, rowcount checked) inside one IMMEDIATE transaction. `db.py gaps --closed` lists closed gaps with the four cells. The audit's CHECK 8 names what a row lacks, not why. Tests T144-11 (now on a fresh replay of the migration files) and T144-14 to T144-23 added; each new case shown red on a seeded defect.

Recorded, not repaired (2026-11-20):
- `emit_batch_sql`'s captured `UPDATE "gaps" ... WHERE "gap_id" = ...` is unguarded, so two sessions' migrations that close the same gap replay with the later one winning (outside this task).
- `gap_mining` (outcome `closure_evidence_found`; `select count(*) from gap_mining where outcome = 'closure_evidence_found'`) already ties a gap to a closing attempt, and `close-gap` does not point at it. It should, once such a row exists: a gap closed by a mining attempt would then name the attempt (a sixth kind, or a typed column) rather than a reason in words. Follow-up.
- A pointer of only U+FFA0, of U+115F with U+1160, or of U+FE0F passes `dbcore.is_blank` and the CHECK: the same class as the open U+034F hole of `dbcore.blank_chars()`. Closing it changes the one blank definition and the spellings pinned in migrations 160, 161 and 162 (tests T078-40, T083-12, T144-01). Follow-up, not done here.
- A NUL inside the session or the pointer is not refused (migrations 160 and 161 leave it open the same way; the CLI cannot pass one); a stamp in the future is not refused by the schema; the not-before-created_at test is skipped on rows whose `created_at` is a date alone (`select count(*) from gaps where length(created_at) = 10`).
- A reason of one character (`x`) is accepted: a reason is free text of non-blank content, as `dbcore.require_reason` reads it.
- The mutant `status LIKE 'CLOSED%'` weakened to `'C%'` cannot be killed: the status column's own CHECK admits only `OPEN%` or `CLOSED%`, so the two are equivalent.

### 12.7 Corrections 2026-11-19, after the adversarial review of this amendment (the lines above stay as written; where they disagree, these govern)

**Correction 1 (12.3 item 2, the location and the run; HIGH).** The whole-token test as written cannot be built and does not close the counterexamples: `retrieval_log.normalise_quote('2015 edition')` returns `'2015edition'` (no tokens), and `python3 -I -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/research');import retrieval_log as R;print(R.phrase_in_quote('5 edition','2015 edition'))"` printed `True` on 2026-11-19, so `--words '5 edition'` would be "found" in a file saying "2015 edition". Replace both tests by ONE boundary rule, one helper in `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py` beside `normalise_quote` (the one home for "a run found at boundaries"), applied twice: the value in the words, and the words in the file.
- **The texts compared.** Each is NFKC-normalised, case-folded and whitespace-collapsed, never made spaceless. The file's text is the saved artefact's text with every `retrieval_log.PAGE_MARKER` line removed and the page of each remaining line recorded from those markers.
- **The boundary, derived from the Unicode database, the same for every script.** A run of `t` is at boundaries when each of its two ends is the start or end of `t` or touches a character whose `unicodedata.category` begins `Z` (space), `P` (punctuation, brackets included) or `S` (symbol), or is `Cc`. No language or script list is typed; no word segmenter is used (adjudication item 58 declined one).
- **What that gives, by script.** Latin and other spaced scripts (Cyrillic, Greek): `5 edition` is not at boundaries in `2015 edition`; `2015 edition` is. Korean, written with spaces: `제3판` is at boundaries in `제3판 발행`, not in `제3판의` (a particle attached: refused, residual). **Scripts written without spaces (Japanese, Chinese; also Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar): a value must be a whole punctuation- or bracket-delimited segment.** For REF-00990's title (`select pub_title from evidence_sources where ref_id='REF-00990'`), `平成十八年政令第三百七十九号` (the bracketed segment) is at boundaries and `十八年…` cut from `平成十八年…` is not. **OPEN POINT and stop condition:** a value shorter than a punctuation-delimited segment in a script written without spaces (an edition such as `第3版` inside `改訂第3版発行`) cannot be recorded by this rule; s

content.content: keys to `perez`) and kept after a letter of any other script; digits folded to ASCII; then `str.casefold` (`ß` to `ss`). Accent folding is part of the ratified key: the ratified words name this normaliser, which folds them. So `Grab Bar`, `grab bar`, `grab-bar` and `grabbar` are **one group**, and `Straße` and `STRASSE` are one group (printed 2026-11-19). **Confirmed by the owner 2026-11-19 (relayed):** "grab bar and grabbar are obviously the same parameter". `casefold` is not locale-aware: Turkish `IŞIK` keys to `isik`, `ışık` to `ısık`, two groups; TR is in no `lang_jur_map` row (`select count(*) from lang_jur_map where upper(language)='TR' or jurisdiction='TR'` printed `(0,)`), so no Turkish form is attestable today: a limit to record if TR is added. The count of a group is all its live attested occurrences in the set. *Reading:* item d's priority only narrows which groups may win.
